description: Work out proportions. Pass `ratio` (golden, root2 or a-series, root3, any a:b such as 3:2 or 16:9, or a decimal such as 1.414; default golden) and `width` or `height`. Optionally `orientation` (landscape by default, or portrait) and `container` (length to split; defaults to the long side). Returns the missing side, the split of the container into a major and minor part at that ratio (with CSS fr and px forms), a table of heights at the same width for ten common ratios, and, when you give both width and height as a source image, centred crop sizes and offsets for the target ratio and common alternatives with the share of area kept. Root-2 is the ISO A-series ratio, where folding a sheet in half keeps its shape. Sources: Graphic Design Solutions (golden section); Samara, Making and Breaking the Grid; Müller-Brockmann, Grid Systems in Graphic Design. That any one ratio is more beautiful is a convention, not a finding. Pure arithmetic, nothing stored.

container.description: Length to split into major and minor parts.

height.description: Known height. Give one of width or height; give both to get crop suggestions.

orientation.description: Landscape (default) makes the width the long side.

ratio.description: golden, root2, a-series, 3:2, 16:9, 4:5, a decimal like 1.414, or any a:b. Default golden.

width.description: Known width in px (or any unit).

name: calculate_proportion
title: Proportion calculator
